mockApiNotice.title: Mock API isn't running
mockApiNotice.why: The Data demo runs only against the template's own Mock API, and only the Demo-specific commands start the Mock API. When you run the app with the regular commands, these pages send no requests, so demo writes never reach a real backend.
mockApiNotice.howToRun: To see the Data demo, run pnpm demo:dev: it starts the Mock API and points the whole app at it, so during that run requests from the real product pages go to the Mock API too.

labRetry.title: Retry rules
labRetry.description: Each button injects a fault into the detail endpoint, then requests it again. A schema mismatch means the frontend and backend contracts have drifted apart, so the global handler logs a SchemaValidationError to the console.
labRetry.succeededAfterRetry: Succeeded on retry after {count, plural, one {# failure} other {# failures}}
labRetry.failedAfterRetry: Failed after {count, plural, one {# retry} other {# retries}}

labConcurrentFailures.title: Simultaneous failures
labConcurrentFailures.description: The button injects 3 failures into the detail endpoint, then refreshes the 3 tasks below at once.

labDraftMode.title: Bypass the server cache
labDraftMode.description: With Draft Mode on, every request from this browser runs use cache functions again, so even a production build shows the backend's latest data right away. Results aren't written to the cache: once you turn it off, you read the data cached before you turned it on. It affects only this browser and resets when the browser closes.
labDraftMode.switchFailed: Couldn't switch. Please try again later.

labQueryStates.title: First load and refresh failures
labQueryStates.description: Render data first, then error, then loading: when a refresh fails, error and the old data exist together, and checking error first would replace data that is still usable.

labSuspenseReset.title: Error boundary and reset
labSuspenseReset.description: The button clears this task's cache and injects one failure, then mounts a component that reads it with useSuspenseQuery.

faultPanel.title: Inject faults
faultPanel.description: “Default latency” applies to every business endpoint, and a fault's latency adds to it. Pick an endpoint and a fault type; the fault disappears once its “times” run out. After injecting one, use other pages and watch how they react.
